summary: In this excerpt from Book 12 (part 45) of a novel, Lexy Moran is alone in her room at dusk after an unsettling moment, looking at herself in the mirror and feeling distraught and desperate. She refuses to come out or eat when Mrs. Royce and Captain Grey knock, and she takes the roses Captain Grey brings from his sister before locking the door again. Left alone in the dark and the chill wind, she wants only to sleep, feeling cut off from the cheerful household downstairs.
one_line: Lexy Moran, distraught and isolated in her room at dusk, refuses visitors and food while longing for sleep.
key_facts: Lexy Moran crosses the room and stands before the mirror as the setting sun falls on her hair, turning it to copper and gold.
Lexy's eyes seem to her enormous, somber, and terrible, and she covers her face with her hands and flings herself on the bed.
When a knock comes at her door, Lexy thrusts her fingers into her ears and lies trembling with her eyes shut tight.
Mrs. Royce calls out that supper is on the table, and Lexy replies that she does not want any supper that night.
Mrs. Royce argues for a time but cannot persuade Lexy even to unlock the door, and goes downstairs with a worried sigh.
Lexy lies in the dark with the window open and the wind blowing chill, too tired to close the window or light the gas.
Captain Grey knocks and asks whether Lexy is ill, then offers her something to eat or a cup of tea; she refuses both.
Captain Grey says he has roses that his sister sent to Lexy and that his sister wanted him to say something to her.
Lexy opens the door suddenly, takes the roses from Captain Grey's hand, says 'Thank you! Good night!' and shuts the door again.
Lexy throws the roses down on the table without putting them in water, saying 'Anything to get rid of him!'
Lexy hears the landlady and Captain Grey talking downstairs and feels shut outside in a black and terrible solitude.
Lexy thinks, 'If I can only sleep!' and hopes that things may look different in the morning.
